unharnessed.meaning: Every duty, condition and qualification survives: GS-12 duties, the Status Candidates announcement, pro rata part-time, probation, background check, Selective Service, PIV with "two forms of ID from the Form i-9", the GS-09 experience, education and combination routes, the 15 semester hours note, and the additional information. "telework" becomes "the chance to work from home", which narrows it slightly.
unharnessed.sense: "all the program goals get ticked off" fits (done), though "ticked off" can also read as annoyed; "postgrad", "pass a background check", "put down how many hours a week" fit. "work from home" narrows "telework".
unharnessed.authenticity: Natural plain Australian: "Here's what the job involves at the GS-12", "part-time work gets counted pro rata", "You've gotta pass a background check", "Have a look at that announcement".
unharnessed.register: A friendly level-3 retelling of a dense federal job ad, with colloquial touches throughout ("If you get picked", "You've gotta", "postgrad") and no swearing. Right weight for a job posting at level 3.
unharnessed.tone: Keeps the job ad's informative, requirement-laden character, just chattier: "You must be a U.S. Citizen or U.S. National."
unharnessed.flow: Reads smoothly: "Manage the work, whether you're doing it on your own, as part of a team, or leading others, so all documents get published on time and accurately".
unharnessed.variety: "get picked", "ticked off", "look after", "pro rata", "put down", "gotta", "spotting and working through", "coming up with fixes", "postgrad"; "You've gotta" twice and "Have a look" twice.
unharnessed.essence: Unmistakably the NARA writer-editor posting, every section in order.

yarn.meaning: Every point survives, carefully: "part-time work is counted pro rata", "born after 31 December 1959", "We offer the chance to telework (work remotely)".
yarn.sense: "new starters", "get through a background check", "Getting information across effectively", "Spotting and analysing production problems" all fit.
yarn.authenticity: Natural Australian plain English: "all new starters in the U.S.", "organisations", "31 December 1959". Nothing forced; very little vernacular.
yarn.register: Mostly Australian-standard plain English with almost no slang ("Please check that announcement for details on the open period, who's eligible, and how to apply."), lighter than level 3.
yarn.tone: The formal-but-plain job ad tone is intact: "You must meet the following requirements by the closing date of this announcement."
yarn.flow: Smooth: "Fill in a Declaration for Federal Employment, when the agency asks for it, so they can decide whether you're suitable for Federal employment."
yarn.variety: Little slang to vary; "picked", "get through", "new starters", "Getting information across"; no repetition noticed.
yarn.essence: Clearly the same job posting, in Australian plain English.

engine.meaning: Near-verbatim, but two swaps change the meaning: "gained in either the punters, private sector or volunteer service" (public sector becomes punters) and "in an appropriate scientific, technical, or social science paddock(s)".
engine.sense: "punters" for "public" (sector) and "paddock(s)" for academic "field(s)" are both wrong senses; "new starters" fits.
engine.authenticity: No Australian would write "social science paddock(s)" or "the punters, private sector"; otherwise the US text is untouched ("Specialized Experience", "Recognizing").
engine.register: Effectively the original ("Properly manipulate the contents of documents and of Federal Register publications"), far below level 3.
engine.tone: The formal tone survives, though "paddock(s)" makes the qualification note faintly ridiculous.
engine.flow: Reads as the original, including its errors ("prior to developed for publication"), plus the jarring "either the punters, private sector".
engine.essence: It is the original posting, unretold.

unharnessed.quote: We offer the chance to work from home, as per Agency policy.
unharnessed.original: We offer opportunities for telework, per Agency policy.
unharnessed.why: Telework can be any remote location, not only home.

unharnessed.quote: all the program goals get ticked off
unharnessed.why: "ticked off" can be read as "annoyed"; "ticked off the list" would be clearer.

yarn.quote: Understand and properly deal with customer needs across every part of the Federal Register publication process, in carrying out the Office of the Federal Register's program responsibilities.
yarn.original: Understand and appropriately address customer needs associated with all aspects of the Federal Register publication process in fulfillment of the Office of the Federal Register's program responsibilities.
yarn.why: Plain rewording with little Aussie flavour; lighter than the level-3 brief.

engine.quote: gained in either the punters, private sector or volunteer service
engine.original: gained in either the public, private sector or volunteer service
engine.why: "public sector" turned into "punters" (customers or gamblers); the eligible experience becomes nonsense.
"paddock" is a farm field, never an academic field.

engine.quote: Properly manipulate the contents of documents and of Federal Register publications to ensure legally effective, timely, and accurate publication of them.
engine.original: Properly manipulate the contents of documents and of Federal Register publications to ensure legally effective, timely, and accurate publication of them.
engine.why: Left untranslated, like nearly all the text.

summaries.unharnessed: A natural, faithful level-3 retelling of a dense job ad.
summaries.yarn: A careful Australian plain-English version, faithful and smooth, but lighter than level 3.
summaries.engine: The original posting with two wrong-sense word swaps ("punters", "paddock") and nothing else retold.
